name: NPrime
statement: def NPrime : Type := { n: Nat // Nat.Prime n } deriving Repr, Ord, LT, LE

name: NPrime.eq_iff
statement: @[simp] theorem NPrime.eq_iff (a b : NPrime) : a = b ↔ a.val = b.val

statement: instance : Dvd NPrime

statement: instance : Coe NPrime Nat

name: PrimeGen
statement:
class PrimeGen (α : Type) where
  P : α → NPrime
  next : α → α
  /-- No prime is skipped between `P g` and `P (next g)`. -/
  hP' (g:α) : (¬∃ q, Nat.Prime q ∧ P g < q ∧  q < P (next g))
  /-- The generated prime strictly increases at each step.
  Needed for infinitude: `hP'` alone allows a constant generator. -/
  hP_lt (g:α) : (P g : Nat) < P (next g)

name: PrimeGt
statement: abbrev PrimeGt (n p:Nat) := Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p

name: MinPrimeGt
statement:
structure MinPrimeGt (n:Nat) where
  p : Nat
  hpgt : PrimeGt n p
  hmin : ∀q:Nat, q < p → (¬ PrimeGt n q)

name: MinPrimeGt.p'
statement: theorem MinPrimeGt.p' (m:MinPrimeGt n) : Nat.Prime m.p

name: fpow
primes
statement:
def primes {α : Type} [pg: PrimeGen α] (g₀ : α) (n : Nat) : List NPrime :=
  fpow (fun g => pg.next g) n g₀ |>.map fun g => pg.P g

name: PrimeGen.P_iterate_add_le
statement:
theorem PrimeGen.P_iterate_add_le {α : Type} [PrimeGen α] (g : α) (k : Nat) :
    (P g : Nat) + k ≤ P (next^[k] g)

name: exists_prime_gt_of_primeGen
statement:
theorem exists_prime_gt_of_primeGen {α : Type} [PrimeGen α] (g₀ : α) (n : Nat) :
    ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p

name: PrimeGen.exists_iterate_P_eq
statement:
theorem PrimeGen.exists_iterate_P_eq {α : Type} [PrimeGen α] (g₀ : α) (q : Nat)
    (hq : Nat.Prime q) (hle : (P g₀ : Nat) ≤ q) : ∃ k, (P (next^[k] g₀) : Nat) = q

name: nosk'
statement: abbrev nosk' P C := (¬∃ q:Nat, Nat.Prime q ∧ P < q ∧ q < C) -- no skipped prime

name: PrimeSieveState
statement:
class PrimeSieveState (α : Type) where
  P     (s:α) : NPrime
  C     (s:α) : Nat
  next  (s:α) (hC: Nat.Prime (C s)) (hN: nosk' (P s) (C s)): α
  hNext (s:α) (hC: Nat.Prime (C s)) (hN: nosk' (P s) (C s)) {s':α}
    : (s'=(next s hC hN) → P s' = C s ∧ C s' > C s)

name: R
statement: def R(P:Nat) : Set Nat := { n | n≥2 ∧ ∀q≤P, Nat.Prime q → ¬q∣n }

name: three_mem_R_two
statement: theorem three_mem_R_two : (3 : Nat) ∈ R 2

name: three_le_of_mem_R_two
statement: theorem three_le_of_mem_R_two : ∀ r ∈ R 2, (3 : Nat) ≤ r

name: r_gt_p
statement: lemma r_gt_p (p:Nat) : (∀r∈R p, r > p)

name: r_next
statement:
theorem r_next (p₀: Nat) (m: MinPrimeGt p₀) {n:Nat}
  : (n ∈ R p₀ ∧ ¬↑m.p ∣ n) ↔ (n ∈ R m.p)

name: r_next_prop
PrimeSieveDriver
statement:
class PrimeSieveDriver (α : Type) [PrimeSieveState α] where
  hCinR  (g:α) : C g ∈ R (P g)            -- C is an element of R
  hRmin  (g:α) : ∀ n ∈ R (P g), C g ≤ n   -- C is min of R

name: c_gt_p
statement: theorem c_gt_p (α : Type) [PrimeSieveState α] [PrimeSieveDriver α] (g:α) : C g > P g

name: no_skipped_prime
statement:
theorem no_skipped_prime (α : Type) [PrimeSieveState α] [PrimeSieveDriver α] (g:α)
  : ¬ ∃ q:Nat, Nat.Prime q ∧ P g < q ∧ q < C g

name: no_prime_factors_im_no_factors
statement:
lemma no_prime_factors_im_no_factors {c:Nat} -- c is a candidate prime
  (h2lc: 2 ≤ c)                              -- c is at least 2
  (hnpf: ∀ p < c, Nat.Prime p → ¬(p∣c))      -- c has no prime factors
  : Nat.Prime c

name: c_prime
statement:
theorem c_prime (α: Type) [PrimeSieveState α] [PrimeSieveDriver α] (g:α)
  : Nat.Prime (C g)

name: hs_suffice
statement:
theorem hs_suffice (α : Type) [PrimeSieveState α] [PrimeSieveDriver α] (g:α)
  :  (Nat.Prime (C g)) ∧ (C g > P g) ∧ (¬∃ q, Nat.Prime q ∧ P g < q ∧  q < C g)

name: nextState
statement:
def nextState {α : Type} [PrimeSieveState α] [PrimeSieveDriver α] (s: α) : α :=
  let c' := c_prime α s
  let ns := no_skipped_prime α s
  PrimeSieveState.next s c' ns

ASeq
statement:
structure ASeq where  -- arithmetic sequence (k + dn)
  k : Nat  -- constant
  d : Nat  -- delta (step size)
deriving Repr

name: ASeq.le
statement: def ASeq.le (a b: ASeq) := if a.d = b.d then a.k≤b.k else a.d<b.d

name: instLEASeq
statement: instance : LE ASeq

name: instTotal

name: instInhabitedASeq

name: aseq
statement: @[simp] def aseq (k:Nat) (d:Nat) := ASeq.mk k d

name: ASeq.nats
statement: def nats  := aseq 0 1

name: ASeq.evens
statement: def evens := aseq 0 2

name: ASeq.odds
statement: def odds  := aseq 1 2

name: ASeq.term
statement: @[simp] def term (s : ASeq) (n : Nat) : Nat := s.k + s.d * n

name: ASeq.instCoeFunASeqNatNat
statement: instance : CoeFun ASeq fun _ => Nat → Nat

name: ASeq.terms
statement: def terms (s : ASeq) (n : Nat) : List Nat := List.range n |>.map λ i => term s i

name: ASeq.compose
statement: def compose (s t: ASeq) : ASeq := aseq (s.k + s.d * t.k) (s.d * t.d)

name: ASeq.compose_def
statement: theorem compose_def (s t: ASeq) {n:Nat} : (s.compose t) n = s (t n)

name: ASeq.partition
statement:
def partition (s : ASeq) (n : Nat) : List ASeq :=
  List.range n |>.map fun i => compose s $ .mk i n

name: ASeq.length_partition
statement:
theorem length_partition {s: ASeq} {n: Nat}
  : (s.partition n).length = n

name: ASeq.instToStringASeq
statement: instance : ToString ASeq

name: ASeq.gte
statement:
def gte (s : ASeq) (n : Nat) : ASeq :=
  if n ≤ s.k then s
  else if n ≤ s.d then .mk (s.k + s.d) s.d
  else
    let t := n / s.d
    ASeq.mk (s.k + s.d * (t + 1)) s.d

name: ASeq.self_lt_mul_div_add
statement: protected lemma self_lt_mul_div_add (n d : Nat) (hd: d > 0) : n ≤ d * (n/d + 1)

name: ASeq.gte_term
statement: theorem gte_term (s : ASeq) (n : Nat) : s.d > 0 → n ≤ term (s.gte n) 0

name: ASeq.gte_same_delta
statement: theorem gte_same_delta (s : ASeq) (n : Nat) : (s.gte n).d = s.d

name: List.Sorted
statement: abbrev Sorted {α : Type _} (r : α → α → Prop) (l : List α) : Prop := l.Pairwise r

name: Rake
statement:
structure Rake : Type where
  d     : Nat
  ks    : List Nat
  size : Nat := ks.length
  sorted: Bool := true
  hsort : sorted → List.Sorted (·<·) ks := by simp
  huniq : sorted → ks.Nodup := by simp
  hsize : 0 < ks.length := by simp

name: Rake.zer
statement: def zer : Rake := { d := 0, ks := [0] }

name: Rake.nat
statement: def nat : Rake := { d := 1, ks := [0] }

name: Rake.ge2
statement: def ge2 : Rake := { d := 1, ks := [2] }

name: Rake.term
statement:
def term (r: Rake) (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  let q := r.ks.length
  have : n%q < r.ks.length := Nat.mod_lt _ r.hsize
  aseq r.ks[n%q] r.d |>.term (n/q)

name: Rake.terms
statement:
def terms (r: Rake) (n: Nat) : List Nat :=
  List.range n |>.map r.term

name: Rake.term_simp
statement:
theorem term_simp (r:Rake) (n:Nat)
: (∃k, (r.term n = k + r.d * (n/r.ks.length)) ∧ ∃i: Fin r.ks.length, i=n%r.ks.length ∧ k=r.ks[i])

name: Rake.term_add_len
statement: theorem term_add_len (r : Rake) (m : Nat) : r.term (m + r.ks.length) = r.term m + r.d

name: Rake.term_iff
statement:
theorem term_iff (r:Rake)
  : ∀m, (∃n, r.term n = m) ↔ (∃ k∈r.ks,  ∃x:Nat, k+x*r.d = m)

name: Rake.seq
statement:
def seq (r:Rake) (n:Nat) {hn:n<r.ks.length} : ASeq :=
  aseq (r.ks[n]'hn) r.d

name: Rake.seqs
statement:
def seqs (r: Rake) : List ASeq :=
  r.ks.map (λ k => aseq k r.d)

name: Rake.k_of_term
statement:
theorem k_of_term (r: Rake) (hmn: r.term m = n)
: ∃k ∈ r.ks, ∃i : (Fin r.ks.length),
    i = m%r.ks.length
    ∧ k = r.ks[i]
    ∧ n = k + r.d * (m/r.ks.length)

Rake.sort

def zero_le_cases (n:Nat) (zeq: 0=n → P) (zlt: 0<n → P) : P :=

name: Rake.length_partition
statement:
theorem length_partition (r:Rake) (j: Nat) (hj:0<j)
  : (r.partition j hj).ks.length = j * r.ks.length

name: Rake.partition_def
statement:
theorem partition_def (r:Rake) (j: Nat) (hj:0<j) (i') (hi')
  : (r.partition j hj).ks[i'] =
    r.ks[i'%r.ks.length]'(List.mod_length r.ks i' r.hsize) + (i'/r.ks.length) * r.d

name: Rake.partition_term_same
statement:
theorem partition_term_same (r:Rake) (j:Nat) (hj: 0 < j) (r':Rake) (hr':r' = r.partition j hj)

name: Rake.partition_term_keep
statement:
theorem partition_term_keep (r:Rake) (j:Nat) (hj: 0 < j) (r':Rake) (hr':r' = r.partition j hj)
  : ∀t, (∃n, r.term n = t) → (∃n, r'.term n = t)

name: Rake.partition_term_iff
statement:
theorem partition_term_iff (r:Rake) (j:Nat) (hj: 0 < j)
  : ∀n, (∃m, (r.partition j hj).term m = n) ↔ (∃m, r.term m = n)

statement: def rem : Rake

name: Rake.HasNonMultiple
statement: abbrev HasNonMultiple (j:Nat): Prop := ∃n, ¬j∣n ∧ ∃m, r.term m=n

name: Rake.rem_def'
statement:
lemma rem_def' (r:Rake) {j: Nat} (hj: 0<j) (r': Rake) (hr': r' = r.rem hj)
  : r'=zer
  ∨ (r'.d=r.d*j ∧ r'.ks=(r.partition j hj).ks.filter (λk => ¬j∣k) ∧ 0<r'.ks.length)

name: Rake.rem_def
statement:
theorem rem_def (r:Rake) {j: Nat} (hj: 0<j) (r': Rake) (hr': r' = r.rem hj) (hnm: HasNonMultiple r j)
  : r'.d=r.d*j ∧ r'.ks=(r.partition j hj).ks.filter (λk => ¬j∣k) ∧ 0<r'.ks.length

name: Rake.rem_drop
statement:
theorem rem_drop (r:Rake) {j: Nat} (hj: 0<j) (r': Rake) (hr': r' = r.rem hj) (hnm: HasNonMultiple r j)
  : ∀n, j∣n → ¬(∃m, r'.term m = n)

name: Rake.rem_keep
statement:
theorem rem_keep (r:Rake) {j: Nat} (hj: 0<j) (r': Rake) (hr': r' = r.rem hj)
  : ∀n, ¬j∣n → (∃m, r.term m = n) → (∃m', r'.term m' = n)

name: Rake.rem_same
statement:
theorem rem_same (r:Rake) {j: Nat} (hj: 0<j) (r': Rake) (hr': r' = r.rem hj) (hnm: HasNonMultiple r j)
  : ∀n, (∃m', r'.term m' = n) → (∃m, r.term m = n)

RakeMap
statement:
structure RakeMap (pred: Nat → Prop) where
  rake : Rake
  hbij : ∀ n, pred n ↔ ∃ m, rake.term m = n
  hord : rake.sorted := by rfl

name: RakeMap.pred
statement: def pred {p:Nat → Prop} (_:RakeMap p) : Nat → Prop := p

name: RakeMap.term
statement: @[simp] def term (rm: RakeMap p) (n:Nat) := rm.rake.term n

name: RakeMap.min_term_zero
statement: theorem min_term_zero (rm:RakeMap p)  : ∀ n, (rm.term 0 ≤ rm.term n)

statement: def rm_ge2 : RakeMap (λn => 2≤n)

name: RakeMap.rem
statement:
def rem (rm : RakeMap prop) (j: Nat) (hj: 0<j) (hnmr: ∃n m, ¬j∣n ∧ rm.term m = n)
  : RakeMap (λ n => prop n ∧ ¬j∣n)

name: RakeMap.rem_d
statement:
theorem rem_d (rm : RakeMap prop) (j : Nat) (hj : 0 < j) (hnmr : ∃ n m, ¬j∣n ∧ rm.term m = n) :
    (rm.rem j hj hnmr).rake.d = rm.rake.d * j

name: RakeSieve
statement:
structure RakeSieve where
  prop : Nat -> Prop
  rm: RakeMap prop
  p : NPrime               -- the current prime
  c : Nat                  -- the candidate for next prime
  hprop : ∀ n:Nat, prop n ↔ n ∈ R p
  hCinR : c ∈ R p
  hRmin : ∀ r ∈ R p, c ≤ r
  -- every prime factor of the rake's period is one of the primes sifted so far.
  -- (the period is their product, p#.) This is what lets the rake prove it never runs empty.
  hdfac : ∀ q, Nat.Prime q → q ∣ rm.rake.d → q ≤ p.val

name: RakeSieve.survivor
statement:
theorem survivor (s : RakeSieve) (hC : Nat.Prime s.c) :
    ∃ n m, ¬ s.c ∣ n ∧ s.rm.term m = n

theorem results_rakeSieve_step (s : RakeSieve) :
    ((nextState s).p : Nat) = s.c ∧ Nat.Prime s.c ∧ (s.p : Nat) < s.c ∧
      ¬ ∃ q, Nat.Prime q ∧ (s.p : Nat) < q ∧ q < s.c
